disclaimer: Model-assisted readings of a single-epoch 15 cm RGB true-orthophoto (Vienna, flights 19/20 March, 29 March and 12 April 2024) at ~10 cm/px. These observations are NOT labelled ground truth, NOT an accuracy or performance measurement, and NOT human validation. Independent human review would be required before operational use. No published value was changed by this audit and none may be changed on the basis of it alone.

reviewers.C: methodology, honesty, schema/output consistency and RGB-supportability audit (no per-building visual reads)

aggregate_framing: Counts below are descriptive over 10 purposively selected buildings. They are not a performance estimate and are not generalisable. n=10 manual spot check, not a validation metric.

review_routing.note: At audit time this building carried a boundary_alignment_warning review flag. Phase 4A showed that warning was measuring interior-ring topology rather than exterior-boundary misalignment; on exterior rings the two estimates are 1.476 m apart, inside the 5.0 m threshold, so the flag no longer fires and the ring-count difference is reported as topology_mismatch instead.

Either way a near-vertical surface lies inside the roof outline, which is visually CONSISTENT WITH section 5 hypotheses 1 and 3 for why SLOPE_MEAN is 42.9 deg on a roof that looks flat. audited_document_provenance: This sha256 is the Phase 2B baseline document the reviewers actually looked at, and is deliberately NOT updated when the pipeline is re-run. The live outputs/roof_attributes.json has since been regenerated (Phase 4A corrections, then the Phase 4B diagnostic rename), so the two hashes differ by design. The current hash is not recorded here because it changes with every regeneration and a stale copy would be worse than none; compute it with `shasum -a 256 outputs/roof_attributes.json` and read what changed in docs/phase3_visual_validation.md. Silently re-pointing this hash would claim the reviewers saw a document that did not exist when they worked.
